newsitem.title: UK: C&W to sell 5.5 percent of HK Telecom to China.
newsitem.headline: C&W to sell 5.5 percent of HK Telecom to China.

text.p: Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc ended months of speculation Friday by agreeing to sell a 5.5 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd to state-owned China Telecom for 726 million pounds ($1.2 billion).
As part of the deal, C&W would have the opportunity to be a major investor in China Telecom (Hong Kong), allowing it to penetrate China's telecommunications market.

"Cable and Wireless is prepared to transfer to China Telecom, in a subsequent phase, further shares in Hong Kong Telecom in expectation of C&W and China Telecom becoming equal shareholders in Hong Kong Telecom," C&W said in a statement.
China Telecom (Hong Kong) is China Telecom's sole vehicle in Hong Kong and was set up to develop activities in the region and in China.
China Telecom operates directly under the control of China's Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications.

"We expect this partnerhsip to deepen and develop further as new opportunities for investment in the China market are identified and quantified," C&W Chief Executive Richard Brown said in the statement. "With this alliance, we now have in place a new platform for substantial and sustained shareholder value creation into the 21st century."

With Hong Kong reverting to Chinese rule at midnight in just 24 days, analysts had expected C&W to sell down its near 59 percent stake in the strategically important Hong Kong group -- in return for growth opportunities on the booming Chinese mainland.
C&W said it would use the cash payment from the sale to reduce its debt.
